title: Mitigate device-resident slab growth during continuous KV warmup via stream-sweep and epoch trimming
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
We observe long-tail growth of device-resident memory in dedicated pools during workloads that continuously warm the KV cache (steady stream of prefix-heavy requests with frequent model variant switches). The allocator (cudaMallocAsync + RTX-pool) is holding multiple pinned staging arenas and partially-empty slabs tied to stream lifetimes. Under mixed batch-size spikes and model-switch churn, the stream-affinity of deferred frees plus our current slab eviction hysteresis prevents timely reclamation, leading to sustained +8-16GB GPU memory delta over baseline after 12+ hours.

Hypothesis:
1) Deferred frees queued on per-stream CUDA free queues plus cross-stream reuse delays cause slabs to remain resident longer than useful, preventing allocator defragmentation.
2) KV prefetching aggressively pins hot KV slices into device-resident slabs; when model variants switch, those slabs become cold but are kept because eviction policy is tied to allocation timestamps and not hotness.
3) Multi-tenant pooling aggregates per-tenant streams into shared arenas; our backpressure logic doesn't signal slab trimming soon enough during throughput drops.

What we've measured so far:
- Reproduced on scale-test (4xA100s) with synthetic KV-warmup profile (50k small requests/hour): memory delta stabilizes at +12.3GB device after 10h compared to baseline.
- Tracing of cudaMallocAsync shows many deferred free events remaining in stream queues for 2-10 seconds before host-side draining.
- Slab residency histogram (from allocator trace) shows a large population of 4MB and 16MB slabs with >90% free space but flagged as resident due to pending CUDA events.
- When forcing cudaDeviceSynchronize periodically, memory drops by ~6GB but throughput suffers ~12% latency regression.

Actions and experiments run (logs/PRs):
- ENG-PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721 - Added an experimental stream-sweep task that opportunistically checks stream event age and triggers async free acceleration when events exceed threshold. (Asha implemented; landed to feature branch).
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/allocator/memory-ephemeral-leak - includes traces and baseline/backfill curves.
- Load test runs: run-2025-02-12A and run-2025-02-14B showing 40-60% reduction in long-tail growth when sweep threshold tuned to 250ms, but increased peak tail latency for rare batches.

Findings so far:
- Stream-sweep reduces long-term residency but trades off with transient latencies for requests that require immediate CUDA syncs; this is unacceptable for strict latency SLO customers.
- Eviction-by-age alone is insufficient; eviction must consider "KV hotness" and per-slab last-access metadata.
- Per-tenant arena consolidation amplified the issue: tenants with bursty warmups prevented global trimming.

Proposed mitigations (short-term and medium-term):
Short-term (hotfix):
- Implement adaptive async-free throttling: detect low request windows per-tenant and trigger background epoch-trim to release slabs older than X seconds and >Y% free. This uses non-blocking cudaStreamQuery + accelerated freeing; PR in review.
- Reduce KV prefetch aggressiveness for low-variance tenants (tune prefetch factor by recent hit-rate).

Medium-term (architectural):
- Add per-slab last-access timestamp and a lightweight LRU eviction for slabs (evict cold, sparse slabs even if cuda events are pending, by migrating small live allocations to a short-lived staging slab before freeing).
- Rework pooling to keep tenant-affine pools when warmup patterns are observed, allowing bulk trimming of cold entire arenas rather than scattering frees across shared pools.
- Kernel-level hinting: expose an API to mark KV slices as migratable so we can compact hot keys into compact slabs proactively.

Open questions / risks:
- Forced migration may amplify short-term allocations and cause temporary fragmentation spike. Need a backpressure strategy to avoid cascading GPU allocation bursts.
- Any solution that relies on periodic cudaDeviceSynchronize or heavy stream syncing risks violating latency SLOs for P0 customers.

Next steps (owners):
- Asha: finish hotfix PR to enable tenant window detection + background epoch trim; run canary on dedicated-dev cluster (due 2025-02-20).
- Liam: instrument per-slab last-access micro-metrics and add to perf dashboard (due 2025-02-18).
- Infra: provision a 6xA100 repro rig for longer 48h runs to validate no regression under mixed-batch and model-switch churn (requested 2025-02-15).

Acceptance criteria:
- Long-term device-resident growth reduced to <4GB after 24h continuous KV warmup in standard repro.
- No >5% regression in P99 latency on steady-state traces when hotfix enabled.
- No increased OOM incidents in Dedicated staging environment for two full 48h runs.
